preconditions.description: The number of queries q is between 1 and 10,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 100 for n, k in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query, n is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= n * (n + 1) // 2 for n, k in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query, k is between 1 and the maximum possible beauty for permutation of length n (n(n+1)/2).

preconditions.expression: queries := [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]
preconditions.description: The input consists of q lines, each containing two integers n and k.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == 'NO' or (output_line == 'YES' and len(permutation) == n) for output_line, n, _ in zip(stdout_lines, [n for n, k in queries], [k for n, k in queries]))
postconditions.description: For each query, if no permutation exists, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by a permutation of length n.

postconditions.expression: all(beauty(permutation) == k for permutation, k in zip(permutations, [k for n, k in queries]))
postconditions.description: If a permutation is output, its beauty must equal the given k.

postconditions.expression: all(set(permutation) == set(range(1, n + 1)) for permutation, n in zip(permutations, [n for n, k in queries]))
postconditions.description: Each permutation must contain all numbers from 1 to n exactly once.
